## Context
The project Jira target is Jira Cloud (`https://navasage.atlassian.net`), while `reconciler.rich_text_cutover` defaults to `off`. Enable the already-shipped and tested Markdown↔ADF bridge behavior for this project without enabling the unrelated Data Center wire. Gerrit CI showed that one legacy plain-wire golden test implicitly inherited the project operational setting; its expected output is intentionally the pre-cutover plain form, so it must select `off` explicitly through the canonical environment override before constructing the real backend.

## Plan
- Add a `[reconciler]` table to the project `rebar.toml` and set `rich_text_cutover = "cloud"`, with an inline `off` rollback note.
- Change `test_canonical_outbound_equivalence.py`’s backend fixture to function scope, accept `monkeypatch`, and set `REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER=off` before constructing `JiraBackend`. Preserve the historical `"LOCAL"` golden expectation.
- Run the exact formerly failing test both normally and with the project configuration active, then run the containing module.
- Run `rebar config`, `git diff --check`, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the repository test gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar.toml` contains `[reconciler]` with `rich_text_cutover = "cloud"` and documents `off` as rollback.
- [x] `rebar config` exits successfully and reports `reconciler.rich_text_cutover = cloud [project]`.
- [x] The legacy equivalence backend fixture explicitly sets the canonical rich-text env override to `off` before backend construction; it does not inherit `rebar.toml`.
- [x] `test_description_change_emits_description` passes with its historical `{description: "LOCAL"}` expectation under the project’s Cloud cutover.
- [x] The containing test module, lint, typecheck, and CI test matrix pass.
- [x] `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors.
